messages:
elena: Heads-up — saw a regression on the 40B stable throughput run after the kernel-selector change. Memory churn up ~22% and tail latency spikes when we have long prompt prefixes. profiler snapshot: 
```
nvtx: allocation stall  -> repeated slab churn (logits scratchpad)
kv-cache: 3x rebinds per request when prefix_len > 512
kernel-affinity: mixed (fp16 fprop, int8 logits) causing extra copies
```
root cause looks like buffer reuse policy not preferring prefix-shaped warm slabs; we keep reallocating logits/scratchpads when different kernels get chosen mid-request. anyone seen this before?

elena: quick repro on canary: run the 8-concurrent long-prefix profile on g4dn. results here: https://perf.internal/shot/8362 :eyes:

matt: interesting — that matches the flamegraphs i pulled earlier. when kernel selector flips kernels between init and decode we lose the pre-warmed slab because keying uses (model, quant) only, not (max_prefix_len, kernel-profile).

matt: short-term hack: pin kernel affinity for warmup path and allocate logits as "prefix_warm" slab keyed by (model, kernel_profile, warm_prefix_bucket). should reduce reallocs.

anya: is there an easy way to make the batching heuristics prefix-aware? current batcher uses median sequence length; long prefixes skew effective scratchpad needs.

elena: yeah — two levers: 1) batcher: compute max prefix per batch and advertise to allocator so cached slabs are selected accordingly, 2) allocator: maintain small LRU per key that includes prefix_bucket (e.g., 0-64,65-256,257-1024).

samir: question: does adding prefix to key blow up memory fragmentation? we might end up keeping many small pools. tradeoff is less churn vs more reserved slabs.

matt: we can cap per-(model,kernel,prefix) pool to N slabs and evict by LRU. experiments show N=2 gives most wins without huge footprint increase.

perf-bot: perf regression detected: throughput -7% on baseline 40B long-prefix test (run 2026-11-17T09:42Z). See details: https://perf.internal/regressions/6263

elena: thanks perf-bot. proposal for an experiment: 
- change allocator key => (model, kernel_profile, prefix_bucket)
- batcher advertises prefix_bucket in request metadata
- pin kernel_affinity for warmup stage to avoid cross-kernel copies
- add fallback: if slab allocation fails, trigger lightweight quant-kernel fallback to avoid OOMs and record metrics
Can we run this on dedicated-canary for 24h?

samir: fine by me. i'll implement the allocator PR and add the per-key cap + eviction. estimate ~2 days.

matt: i'll add batcher change and a flag `batcher.prefix_aware=true` so we can A/B. also add a trace tag so console can show prefix-bucket histograms per route.

anya: if we do per-key pools we should update the optimize heuristics to recommend a prefix_bucket target for heavy-route users — they tend to have consistent prefix shapes.

elena: plan accepted. samir + matt, coordinate on API for the advertized prefix_bucket (simple int in RequestMeta). I'll open a canary ticket and add test script for long-prefix mixture.

deploy-bot: canary created: canary/allocator-prefix-aware-2026-11-18T03:00Z by elena. CI link: https://ci.internal/builds/99812

matt: quick note for observability — add metric `allocator.reuse_hits{prefix_bucket}` and a tracing span for "slab.key_lookup". we want to show reduced slab churn in dash.

elena: awesome. if we see >80% reuse_hits and tail-latency down 15% we merge. otherwise rollback. will post results here. :rocket:
